idiom_name: significant indentation with the PEP 8 four-space step, normalized by Black
implementation_notes: Python is the case where the rectangle is the syntax: a suite is a colon plus an indented region, so block extent cannot be ambiguous, and PEP 8 fixes the step at four spaces per level (spaces preferred, and the parser rejects tabs and spaces mixed inconsistently). What is left of the pattern is depth and wrapping - early returns and with/comprehension forms keep suites shallow, and Black normalizes the remaining layout deterministically (line length 88, stable wrapping), so the shape is not a discussion. The classic hand-formatted form is meaningful only inside a codebase that runs no formatter; there, match the file.
pitfalls: Black and PEP 8 disagree on line length (88 versus 79) and on call wrapping; configuring both produces churn, so choose one and ignore the other's cosmetic rules.
Deeply indented code can still be under 88 columns and pass every linter: nothing measures nesting depth, so the depth budget has to be enforced by review or extraction.
Tabs are only tolerated while they are consistent within a file; switching a tab-indented module to spaces reformats it entirely and makes review diffs unreadable.
